Generate synthetic respondents with language models

Source: R/generate.R
generate_synthetic.Rd

Experimental. generate_synthetic() asks one or more language models to take an instrument as each persona and returns one row per synthetic respondent. Each call makes one respondent: The persona is the system prompt, and the instructions, the response scale and the items are the user prompt (see sc_prompt()). The model answers in structured JSON, one whole number per item.

Usage

generate_synthetic(
  instrument,
  models,
  personas = NULL,
  attempts = 1,
  respondents = 1,
  batch_size = 1,
  block_size = NULL,
  shuffle = FALSE,
  max_retries = 2,
  parallel = 1,
  output = NULL,
  format = c("csv", "json", "rds", "xlsx"),
  progress = interactive(),
  progress_file = NULL,
  stop_file = NULL,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

instrument

an sc_instrument().

models

one sc_model() or a list of them.

personas

an sc_personas() table, a character vector of descriptions, or NULL for respondents without a persona.

attempts

number of attempts per model.

respondents

number of respondents per persona in each attempt.

batch_size

number of respondents per call. The default, 1, keeps every respondent independent. A larger batch asks one call for several respondents of the same persona: That is cheaper, but the respondents in a batch may depend on each other (the model sees its own earlier answers), which can make them look more alike or more deliberately different than independent people would.

block_size

ask at most this many items per call. A respondent's blocks are asked one after another in the same conversation. NULL asks all items at once.

shuffle

shuffle the item order for each call?

max_retries

how often to retry a call that fails or gives invalid answers.

parallel

number of calls to run at the same time.

output

optional folder to write the data to.

format

file format for output: "csv", "json", "rds" or "xlsx" (needs writexl).

progress

show a progress bar with the time left in the console? A function also works: It is called after every respondent with a list (done, total, failed, elapsed, eta in seconds, and so on).

progress_file

optional path of a JSON file updated after every respondent (used by run_synthcheck_app()).

stop_file

optional path: When this file appears, the run stops after the calls in progress and returns what is done.

seed

random seed for shuffling and for the mock provider.

Value

A tibble with model, provider, model_id, temperature, attempt, persona_id, respondent, any persona attributes, and one column per item. The attribute log holds the failed calls.

Details

An attempt is one full pass over the personas, with respondents respondents per persona, as in hexaco_llm. The number of calls is the number of models times attempts times the number of personas times respondents. Answers outside the scale, missing items and failed calls are retried up to max_retries times and then stored as NA.

With output, each attempt is written to its own file as soon as it is done, with run.json (the settings, without API keys) and prompts.json (every prompt sent) beside it, so a stopped run keeps the finished attempts. Read the folder back with read_synthetic().

Synthetic respondents are experimental: Use them to compare models with authenticity_benchmark(), not to replace a field test.

See also

sc_instrument(), sc_personas(), sc_model(), as_synthetic_list(), authenticity_benchmark()

Examples

ins <- sc_instrument(hexaco_items[hexaco_items$trait == "H", ], scale = c(1, 7))
per <- sc_persona_grid(age = c(25, 65), template = "You are {age} years old.")
syn <- generate_synthetic(ins, sc_model("mock"), per, attempts = 2, respondents = 3)
syn
#> # A tibble: 12 × 48
#>    model provider model_id temperature attempt persona_id respondent   age
#>    <chr> <chr>    <chr>          <dbl>   <int> <chr>           <int> <dbl>
#>  1 mock  mock     mock               1       1 p001                1    25
#>  2 mock  mock     mock               1       1 p001                2    25
#>  3 mock  mock     mock               1       1 p001                3    25
#>  4 mock  mock     mock               1       1 p002                1    65
#>  5 mock  mock     mock               1       1 p002                2    65
#>  6 mock  mock     mock               1       1 p002                3    65
#>  7 mock  mock     mock               1       2 p001                1    25
#>  8 mock  mock     mock               1       2 p001                2    25
#>  9 mock  mock     mock               1       2 p001                3    25
#> 10 mock  mock     mock               1       2 p002                1    65
#> 11 mock  mock     mock               1       2 p002                2    65
#> 12 mock  mock     mock               1       2 p002                3    65
#> # ℹ 40 more variables: HSinc1 <int>, HSinc2 <int>, HSinc3 <int>, HSinc4 <int>,
#> #   HSinc5 <int>, HSinc6 <int>, HSinc7 <int>, HSinc8 <int>, HSinc9 <int>,
#> #   HSinc10 <int>, HFair1 <int>, HFair2 <int>, HFair3 <int>, HFair4 <int>,
#> #   HFair5 <int>, HFair6 <int>, HFair7 <int>, HFair8 <int>, HFair9 <int>,
#> #   HFair10 <int>, HGree1 <int>, HGree2 <int>, HGree3 <int>, HGree4 <int>,
#> #   HGree5 <int>, HGree6 <int>, HGree7 <int>, HGree8 <int>, HGree9 <int>,
#> #   HGree10 <int>, HMode1 <int>, HMode2 <int>, HMode3 <int>, HMode4 <int>, …
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY
syn <- generate_synthetic(ins, list(sc_model("anthropic"), sc_model("openai")), per,
                          attempts = 5, respondents = 10, parallel = 8,
                          output = "hexaco_run")
} # }
